nifo/eis.head: νιφόεις
nifo/eis.html: νιφόεις -εντος πνίφω.] Snowclad, snowcapt : ὄρεϊ Il. 13.754. Cf. Il. 14.227, Il. 18.616, Il. 20.385 : Od. 19.338.

nw/numnos.head: νώνυμνος
nw/numnos.html: νώνυμνος -ον [ = νώνυμος.] 1 = νώνυμος. (1) Il. 12.70= Il. 13.227= Il. 14.70. 2 Undistinguished, obscure, inglorious : γενεήν Od. 1.222.

naieta/w.head: ναιετάω
naieta/w.html: ναιετάω [in form frequentative fr. ναίω1.] Fem. pple. ναιετάουσα, -ης, ναιετόωσα, -ης Il. 2.648, Il. 3.387, Il. 6.415 : Od. 1.404, Od. 8.574. 3 sing. pa. iterative ναιετάασκε Il. 11.673, Il. 17.308 : Od. 15.385. 3 pl. ναιετάασκον Il. 2.539, 841. (περι-) 1 To live, dwell, abide, have one's home : λακεδαίμονι ναιετοώσῃ (in . . .) Il. 3.387. Cf. Il. 7.9, Il. 11.673 : Od. 6.153, 245, Od. 15.255, 360, 385, Od. 17.523. 2 Of cities, by a sort of personification, to stand, have their place : Ἰθάκης ἔτι ναιεταούσης (while . . .stands) Od. 1.404. Cf. Il. 4.45. So of islands, to lie Od. 9.23. Sim. with εὖ, of cities, houses, etc., to have a fair exposure or aspect, be pleasant to dwell in : πόλεις εὖ ναιετοώσας Il. 2.648, δόμους εὖ ναιετάοντας Il. 6.370= 497, Il. 11.769. Cf. Il. 6.415 : Od. 2.400, Od. 4.96, Od. 8.574, Od. 17.28, 85 = 178, 275, 324= Od. 21.242, Od. 19.30 = Od. 21.387, Od. 20.371, Od. 22.399, Od. 24.362. 3 To live in, dwell in, have one's home in, inhabit, hold, have : Ἰθάκην Od. 9.21. Cf. Il. 2.539, 841, Il. 17.172, 308.

neme/qw.head: νεμέθω
neme/qw.html: νεμέθω [νέμω.] In mid., of birds, to take their food, peck : πελειάδες νεμέθοντο Il. 11.635.

neu=ron.head: νεῦρον
neu=ron.html: νεῦρον -ου, τό [cf. νευρή.] 1 A tendon : νεῦρα διεσχίσθη Il. 16.316. 2 In pl. with collective sense=νευρή.: ἕλκε νεῦρα βόεια Il. 4.122. 3 A string whipping the head of an arrow to the shaft : ν. τε καὶ ὄγκους Il. 4.151.

nau/maxos.head: ναύμαχος
nau/maxos.html: ναύμαχος [ναυ-, νηῦς + μάχομαι.] Intended to be used in sea-fighting Il. 15.389, 677.

nika/w.head: νικάω
nika/w.html: νικάω [νίκη.] 1 pl. pa. iterative νικάσκομεν Od. 11.512. 1 To overcome, vanquish, get the better of, in fight or in a contest : δοκέω νικησέμεν Ἕκτορα Il. 7.192, ἀνδρὶ νικηθέντι γυναῖκʼ ἔθηκεν (as a prize for the loser) Il. 23.704. Cf. Il. 3.404, Il. 13.318, Il. 16.79, Il. 20.410, Il. 21.501, Il. 23.634, 680, 756:Od. 13.261, Od. 18.83, 333 = 393. 2 Absol., to be the conqueror, prove the winner, in fight or in a contest Il. 3.439, Il. 4.389, Il. 5.807, Il. 20.102, Il. 23.669, Il. 3.71 = 92 : = Od. 18.46, Od. 8.520, Od. 11.548. In aor. pple., the winner : ρῷ κε νικήσαντι κεκλήσῃ ἄκοιτις Il. 3.138. Cf. Il. 3.255, Il. 23.702. In aor. pple. pass., the loser: τῷ νικηθέντι τίθει δέπας Il. 23.656. Cf. Il. 23.663. 3 In gen., to overcome, get the better of : νόον κίκησε νεοίη (overcame your better judgment) Il. 23.604. Cf. Od. 18.319. With cognate acc.: νίκης, τήν μιν ἐγὼ νίκησα (i. e. I won the cause) Od. 11.545. 4 To excel, be first or pre-eminent among, bear away the palm from : ἀγορῇ ἑ παῦροι νίκων Il. 15.284. Cf. Il. 9.130, 272 : Od. 11.512. 5 Absol., to be first or pre-eminentm bear the palm Il. 2.370, 597, Il. 18.252: Od. 3.121. Of an inanimate object: κάλλει ἐνίκα [κρητήρ] (in . . .) Il. 23.742. Of abstractions, to prevail, rule, carry it away : βουλὴ κακὴ νίκησεν Od. 10.46. Cf. Il. 1.576 : = Od. 18.404.

neio/qi.head: νειόθι
neio/qi.html: νειόθι [-θι. Cf. νέατος, νείατος.] At the bottom of. With genit. : ν. λίμνης Il. 21.317.

nu/ssw.head: νύσσω
nu/ssw.html: νύσσω 3 sing. aor. νύξε Il. 5.46, Il. 11.96, Il. 12.395, Il. 15.536, Il. 16.404, Il. 23.819, etc. Pple. νύξας Od. 14.485. 1 To wound, pierce or strike by a thrust with a pointed weapon, make a thrust at with such a weapon : τὸν ἔγχεϊ νύξε κατὰ δεξιὸν ὦμον Il. 5.46. Cf. Il. 11.96, Il. 15.536, Il. 16.346, Il. 20.397, etc. Without expressed object Il. 11.235= Il. 17.48, Il. 13.147 = Il. 15.278= Il. 17.731, Il. 23.819. Sim. in mid. of reciprocal action Il. 14.26= Il. 16.637. 2 App. implying no more than striking with the hand : χείρεσσʼ ἀσπίδα νύσσων Il. 16.704. 3 To give one a nudge (with the elbow) : ἀγκῶνι νύξας Od. 14.485.

na/ph.head: νάπη
na/ph.html: νάπη -ης, ἡ. A valley or glen : ἔκ τʼ ἔφανεν νάπαι Il. 8.558= Il. 16.300.

nh/pios.head: νήπιος
nh/pios.html: νήπιος -η, -ον. 1 Young, of tender years : τέκνα Il. 2.136. Cf. Il. 4.238, Il. 5.480, Il. 6.400, Il. 9.440, Il. 16.8, etc. : Od. 2.313, Od. 4.818, Od. 6.301, Od. 11.449, Od. 19.530, etc. In reference to the young of a bird or animal Il. 2.311, Il. 11.113. Absol. in neut. pl. νήπια, the young of an animal: λέων, ᾧ νἡπιʼ ἄγοντι . . . Il. 17.134. 2 Such as a child's is, feeble : βίη νηπίη [ἐστίν] Il. 11.561. 3 Childish, foolish, thoughtless, senseless, credulous : φῆ αἱρήσειν πόλιν, ν. Il. 2.38. Cf. Il. 2.873, Il. 5.406, Il. 7.401, Il. 16.46, Il. 18.311, Il. 22.445 (fond heart), etc. : Od. 1.8, Od. 3.146, Od. 4.31, Od. 9.44, Od. 21.85, etc. In voc. νήπιε Il. 16.833, Il. 18.295, Il. 21.99, Il. 22.333. Absol. in masc., a fool : ῥεχθὲν ν. ἔγνω Il. 17.32 = Il. 20.198. In neut. pl., foolish things, folly : νήπια βάζεις Od. 4.32.

ni=sa.head: Νῖσα
ni=sa.html: Νῖσα (ζαθέη). A Boeotian town Il. 2.508.

neoteuxh/s.head: νεοτευχής
neoteuxh/s.html: νεοτευχής [νέος + τεύχω.] Newly made or constructed, new : δίφροι Il. 5.194.

nearo/s.head: νεαρός
nearo/s.html: νεαρός [νέος.] Young : παῖδες Il. 2.289.

ne/mesis.head: νέμεσις
ne/mesis.html: νέμεσις ἡ. Dat. νεμέσσι Il. 6.335. 1 Righteous indignation or vexation, blame, censure, reproach : ἐν φρεσὶ θέσθε νέμεσιν (i. e. the fear of it) Il. 13.122. Cf. Il. 6.335, 351 : ν. μοι ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἔσσεται Od. 2.136. Cf. Od. 22.40. 2 Something worthy of righteous indignation or of blame, censure or reproach. With infin. (cf. χάρις 4..b): οὐ ν. Τρῶας καὶ Ἀχαιοὺς ἄλγεα πάσχειν (small blame to them if they . . . ) Il. 3.156. Cf. Il. 14.80 : Od. 1.350, Od. 20.330.

neka/s.head: νεκάς
neka/s.html: νεκάς ἡ [cf. νέκυς.] Dat. pl. νεκάδεσσι. A heap of slain : ἐν αἰνῇσιν νεκάδεσσιν Il. 5.886.

ne/ktar.head: νέκταρ
ne/ktar.html: νέκταρ -αρος, τό. The drink of the gods Il. 1.598, Il. 4.3 : Od. 5.93, 199, Od. 9.359. Introduced by divine agency into the corpse of Patroclus Il. 19.38. Into Achilles Il. 19.347, 353.

nhrhi/s.head: νηρηΐς
nhrhi/s.html:
νηρηΐς -ίσος [fem. patronymic fr. Νηρεύς.] A daughter of Nereus, a Nereïd or sea-nymph Il. 18.38, 49, 52.
Νηρηΐς See Lexicon. Νηρεύς͂ the ἅλιος γέρων of Il. 1.556 : Od. 24.58, and the πατὴρ γέρων and γέρων ἅλιος of Il. 18.36, 141.

neh/khs.head: νεήκης
neh/khs.html: νεήκης [νέος + *ἀκή = ἀκωκή.] Newly sharpened : πελέκεσσι νεήκεσιν Il. 13.391 = Il. 16.484.

nhlhia/dhs.head: Νηληϊάδης
nhlhia/dhs.html: Νηληϊάδης Patronymic from prec. Of Nestor Il. 8.100 , Il. 10.87, 555, Il. 11.511, 618, Il. 14.42, Il. 15.378, Il. 23.303 : Od. 3.79, 202, 247, 465.

ne/atos.head: νέατος
ne/atos.html: νέατος νείατος -η [superl. Cf. νείαιρα, νειόθεν, νειόθι. App. not conn. with νέ(ϝ)ος.] 1 Lowest, the lowest : ἔκειτο νείατος ἄλλων Il. 6.295 : = Od. 15.108. Cf. Il. 2.824, Il. 8.478. The lowest part of : παρὰ νείατον ἀνθερεῶνα Il. 5.293. Cf. Il. 5.857, Il. 11.381, Il. 15.341, Il. 16.821, Il. 17.310. 2 Extreme, outermost, the extreme or outermost : [πόλεις] νέαται πύλου Il. 9.153 = 295. Cf. Il. 11.712 : παρὰ νείατον ὄρχον Od. 7.127.– Forming the extremity of a row, the extreme or last : τὸν ἔβαλεν νείατον ἀστράγαλον Il. 14.466 (here, contextually, the highest).

nekro/s.head: νεκρός
nekro/s.html: νεκρός -οῦ, ὁ [cf. νέκυς.] 1 A dead body, a corpse Il. 4.467, Il. 5.620, Il. 7.332, Il. 13.194, Il. 17.13, Il. 21.235, etc.: Od. 12.10, 13. 2 The spirit of a dead man conceived of as departing from the body : ὅσσʼ ἐπιεικὲς νεκρὸν ἔχοντα νέεσθαι ὑπὸ ζόφον Il. 23.51. In pl., the shades of the departed, the dead: ἔθνεα νεκρῶν Od. 10.526, Od. 11.34, 632. Cf. Od. 11.475.

nh/dumos.head: νήδυμος
nh/dumos.html: νήδυμος [no doubt (ϝ)ήδυμος = ἡδύς (cf. καλός, κάλλιμος) with adhesion of ν transferred from preceding words. Cf. Eng. newt (for ewt, with n- fr. an), and nickname (for eke-name, with sim. n-).] Epithet of sleep, sweet, grateful, refreshing ( = ἡδύς (2)) Il. 2.2, Il. 10.91, 187, Il. 14.242, 253, 354, Il. 16.454, Il. 23.63 : Od. 4.793, Od. 12.311, 366, Od. 13.79.

nhmerth/s.head: νημερτής
nhmerth/s.html:
νημερτής -ές [νη- + ἁμαρτ-, ἁμαρτάνω.] 1 Unerring, having or speaking with perfect knowledge Od. 4.349 = Od. 17.140, Od. 4.384, 401, 542. Infallibly purposed, that shall not fail : βουλήν Od. 1.86, Od. 5.30. 2 Consonant with reality, true : μὴ πάντα νημερτέα εἶπεν (that it was all true that she said) Od. 5.300. Cf. Il. 3.204 : Od. 11.137, Od. 17.549, 556, 561. 3 Absol. in neut. pl. νημερτέα, the truth : νημερτέα μυθήσασθε Il. 6.376. Cf. Od. 3.19, Od. 11.96, Od. 15.263. 4 In neut. sing. νημερτές as adv. a Clearly, plainly, so that no mistake may be made : ἐνίσπες Od. 22.166. b Truly : ὑπόσχεο Il. 1.514. Cf. Il. 14.470 : Od. 3.101 = Od. 4.327, Od. 4.314, 642, Od. 11.148, Od. 12.112, Od. 23.35. 5 In neut. pl. νημερτέα as adv., with certainty, clearly : ἐπεὶ τῶν νόον νημερτέʼ ἀνέγνω Od. 21.205.
Νημερτής A Nereid Il. 18.46 .

nireu/s.head: Νιρεύς
nireu/s.html: Νιρεύς Son of Charopus and Aglaia and leader of the men of Syme. His beauty Il. 2.671-673.

nu=n.head: νῦν
nu=n.html: νῦν 1 At the present time, now : οἷοι νῦν βροτοί εἰσιν Il. 5.304. Cf. Il. 1.109, Il. 2.254, Il. 7.129, Il. 12.271, etc. : Od. 1.82, Od. 3.69, Od. 17.245, Od. 18.239, etc. At the present time, on the present occasion, now, as opposed in terms to the past or future : ἢ νῦν δηθύνοντʼ ἢ ὕστερον αὖτις ἰόντα Il. 1.27. Cf. Il. 1.455, Il. 3.439, Il. 4.321, etc. : τὸ πρίν : ἀτὰρ μὲν νῦν γε . . . Od. 4.32. Cf. Od. 1.369, Od. 3.366, Od. 6.243, etc. 2 In the time following more or less directly the present, now : νῦν δʼ εἶμι φθίηνδε Il. 1.169. Cf. Il. 1.59, 421, Il. 2.12, Il. 7.226, etc. : Od. 1.200, Od. 2.314, Od. 3.359, Od. 4.685, etc. 3 Looking back to an occurrence in the past, now : ὃς νῦν Ἀργείοισι κήδεʼ ἐφῆκεν Il. 1.445. Cf. Il. 1.506, Il. 2.274, Il. 4.12, Il. 13.772, etc. : Od. 1.35, 43, Od. 2.28, Od. 6.172, etc. So in a past supposition contrary to fact : νῦν ἂν ὕστατα λωβήσαιο Il. 1.232 = Il. 2.242. 4 νῦν δέ, but as it is : τιμήν μοι ὄφελλεν ἐγγυαλίξαι · νῦν δʼ οὐδέ με τυτθὸν ἔτεισεν Il. 1.354. Cf. Il. 1.417, Il. 2.82, Il. 9.519, Il. 12.326, etc. : Od. 1.166, Od. 2.79, Od. 14.371, Od. 18.403, etc. 5 In sentences expressing a command, request, exhortation or wish, with the temporal sense weakened or effaced, now : νῦν ἐμέθεν ξύνες ὦκα Il. 2.26. Cf. Il. 1.407, Il. 5.129, Il. 14.219, Il. 21.428, etc. : νῦν μήτʼ εἴης μήτε γένοιο Od. 18.79. Cf. Od. 1.271, Od. 2.281, Od. 4.395, Od. 8.202, Od. 10.320, Od. 11.441, etc. 6 Continuing an enumeration, now, and now : νῦν αὖ τοὺς ὅσσοι . . . τῶν αὖ ἦν ἀρχὸς Ἀχιλλεύς Il. 2.681. 7 In a question, well now : πῶς γὰρ νῦν . . . ; Il. 10.424. Cf. Od. 18.223.

neo/smhktos.head: νεόσμηκτος
neo/smhktos.html: νεόσμηκτος [νέος + σμήχω.] Newly burnished or polished : θωρήκων Il. 13.342.

nhleu/s.head: Νηλεύς
nhleu/s.html: Νηλεύς (ἀγαυότατος ζωόντων, ἀμύμων , ἀντίθεος, θεόφιν μήστωρ ἀτάλαντος, κρατερὸς θεράπων Διός, μεγάθυμος). Son (Od. 11.241) of Poseidon and Tyro, husband of Chloris and (Od. 11.285) father of Nestor, Chromius-1, Periclymenus and Pero (in Il. 11.692 he is said to have had twelve sons) Il. 11.683, 717 : Od. 3.4, 409, Od. 11.254, 281; his requirement of Pero's suitors Od. 11.288; his treatment of Melampus Od. 15.229, 233.

neio/qen.head: νειόθεν
neio/qen.html: νειόθεν [-θεν 1. Cf. νέατος, νείατος.] From the bottom : ν. ἐκ κραδίης (from the bottom of his heart) Il. 10.10.

no/tos.head: νότος
no/tos.html: νότος -ου, ὁ. 1 The south wind Il. 2.145 (see under εὖρος), Il. 2.395, Il. 3.10, Il. 11.306, Il. 16.765, Il. 21.334 : Od. 3.295, Od. 5.295, 331, Od. 12.289, 325, 326, 427. 2 The south : πρὸς νότου Od. 13.111.

na/w.head: νάω
na/w.html: νάω (σνάϝω). To flow Il. 21.197 : Od. 6.292.

nefelhgere/ta.head: νεφεληγερέτα
nefelhgere/ta.html: νεφεληγερέτα [νεφέλη + ἀγείρω.] (Prob. orig. a voc. turned into a nom., from which the genit. νεφεληγερέταο (Il. 5.631, 736, Il. 8.387, Il. 15.154, Il. 20.10, Il. 21.499) is formed.) The cloud-gatherer. Epithet of Zeus Il. 1.511, 560, Il. 5.631, Il. 7.280, Il. 11.318, Il. 15.154, etc.: Od. 1.63 = Od. 5.21 = Od. 24.477, Od. 9.67, Od. 12.313, 384 = Od. 13.139 = 153.

neio/s.head: νειός
neio/s.html: νειός -οῦ, ἡ [νέος.] A fallow field (in process of being ploughed up) : ἑλκέμεναι νειοῖο ἄροτρον (genit. of space) Il. 10.353. Cf. Il. 13.703, Il. 18.541, 547 : Od. 5.127, Od. 8.124, Od. 13.32.

ne/fos.head: νέφος
ne/fos.html: νέφος τό [cf. νεφέλη.] Dat. pl. νεφέεσσι Il. 5.867, Il. 17.594 : Od. 5.293, 303, Od. 9.68, Od. 16.264, etc. νεφεσσι Il. 13.523. A cloud : ν. ἐρχόμενον κατὰ πόντον Il. 4.275, νέφεα σκιόεντα Il. 5.525. Cf. Il. 5.751, Il. 11.28, 62, Il. 15.170, Il. 17.372, Il. 23.213, etc. : Od. 5.293, 303, Od. 8.374, Od. 9.68 = Od. 12.314, Od. 9.145, Od. 11.592, Od. 16.264, Od. 20.104, 114, Od. 22.304. A cloud or body of mist : τοῖόν τοι ν. ἀμφικαλύψω Il. 14.343. Cf. Il. 15.153, 668, Il. 18.205, Il. 23.188. Fig. : θανάτου ν. Il. 16.350. Cf. Il. 17.243 : Od. 4.180. Also ν. εἵπετο πεζῶν Il. 4.274, Il. 23.133. Cf. Il. 16.66, Il. 17.755.

nu/mfh.head: νύμφη
nu/mfh.html: νύμφη -ης, ἡ. Voc. νύμφα Il. 3.130 : Od. 4.743. 1 A young woman, a maiden Il. 9.560. 2 A nymph, one of a class of semi-divine female beings imagined as inhabiting the sea, fountains, islands, caves, etc. : νυμφάων, αἵ τʼ ἄλσεα νέμονται καὶ πηγὰς ποταμῶν καὶ πίσεα Il. 20.8. Cf. Il. 24.616 : Od. 1.71, Od. 6.105, 123, Od. 9.154, Od. 12.132, 318, Od. 13.107, 350, 355, Od. 14.435, Od. 17.211, 240. Of Calypso Od. 1.14, 86, Od. 4.557 = Od. 5.14 = Od. 17.143, Od. 5.6, 30, 57, 149, 153, 196, 230 = , Od. 23.333. Of Circe Od. 10.543. Defined by νηΐς Il. 6.21, Il. 14.444, Il. 20.384. By ὀρεστιάς Il. 6.420. By νηϊάς Od. 13.104 = 348, 356. 3 A bride, a woman about to be married Il. 18.492. 4 A bride, a woman not long married Od. 11.38, 447. Applied to matrons. To Helen Il. 3.130. To Penelope Od. 4.743.

neosso/s.head: νεοσσός
neosso/s.html: νεοσσός -οῦ, ὁ [νέος.] A young bird, anestling : στρουθοῖο νεοσσοί Il. 2.311. Cf. Il. 9.323.

nhga/teos.head: νηγάτεος
nhga/teos.html: νηγάτεος Of unknown origin and meaning : χιτῶνα Il. 2.43, κρηδέμνῳ Il. 14.185.

nh=stis.head: νῆστις
nh=stis.html: νῆστις [νη-εδ-τις, νη- + ἐδ-, ἔδω.] Without eating, fasting Il. 19.156, 207 : Od. 18.370.

nifeto/s.head: νιφετός
nifeto/s.html: νιφετός ὁ [νίφω.] Snow Il. 10.7 : Od. 4.566.

no/tios.head: νότιος
no/tios.html: νότιος [νότος.] 1 Flowing, running : ἱδρώς Il. 11.811, Il. 23.715. 2 Absol. as sb., the part towards the south : ὑψοῦ ἐν νοτίῳ νῆʼ ὅρμισαν Od. 4.785, Od. 8.55 (i.e. just outside the haven (which is thought of as facing south) to await the evening landbreeze).

nhe/w.head: νηέω
nhe/w.html: νηέω (ἐπινηνέω, παρανηνέω.) To heap or pile up: ὕλην Il. 23.139, 163. Cf. Il. 23.169, Il. 24.276 : ξύλα πολλά Od. 19.64. To heap up (a fire), make a good (fire) : πῦρ εὖ νηῆσαι Od. 15.322. To heap (a ship) full, give (her) a full cargo Il. 9.358. In mid. Il. 9.137, 279.

nhleh/s.head: νηλεής
nhleh/s.html: νηλεής -ές [νη- + ἔλεος.] With hyphaeresis νηλής Il. 9.632. Dat. νηλέϊ Il. 3.292, Il. 5.330, Il. 13.501, Il. 16.345, Il. 19.266, etc.: Od. 4.743, Od. 8.507, Od. 9.272, Od. 12.372, Od. 22.475, etc. Acc. νηλέα Il. 19.229. Pitiless, ruthless, relentless, showing no feeling for others, hard : ἦτορ Il. 9.497. Cf. Il. 9.632 : Od. 9.272 = 368, Od. 9.287. Absol. in voc. : νηλεές Il. 16.33, 204. So νηλέα θυμὸν ἔχοντας (steeling our hearts) Il. 19.229. Applied to δεσμός Il. 10.443. To ὕπνος (as bringing mischief upon one) Od. 12.372. For νηλεὲς ἦμαρ see ἦμαρ 4.g. Epithet of χαλκός Il. 3.292, Il. 4.348, Il. 5.330, Il. 12.427, Il. 13.501 = Il. 16.761, Il. 13.553, Il. 16.345, 561, Il. 17.376, Il. 19.266 : Od. 4.743, Od. 8.507, Od. 10.532, Od. 11.45, Od. 14.418, Od. 18.86, Od. 21.300, Od. 22.475.

nu/ssa.head: νύσσα
nu/ssa.html: νύσσα -ης, ἡ [νύσσω. The scratch.] 1 The starting-line in a race : τοῖσιν ἀπὸ νύσσης τέτατο δρόμος Il. 23.758 : Od. 8.121. 2 The turning-post : ἐν νύσσῃ τοι ἵππος ἀριστερὸς ἐγχριμφθήτω Il. 23.338. Cf. Il. 23.332, 344.

nai/.head: ναί
nai/.html: ναί Emphasizing affirmative particle, truly, of a surety. Followed by δή Il. 1.286= Il. 8.146= Il. 24.379, Il. 10.169, Il. 18.128, Il. 23.626 : Od. 4.266, Od. 18.170, Od. 20.37, Od. 22.486. In an affirmation, followed by μά Il. 1.234.

nefe/lh.head: νεφέλη
nefe/lh.html: νεφέλη -ης, ἡ [cf. νέφος.] A cloud : ἐν αἰθέρι καὶ νεφέλῃσιν Il. 15.20, 192. Cf. Il. 2.146, Il. 5.522, Il. 16.298: Od. 5.291, Od. 12.74, 405 = Od. 14.303. A cloud or body of mist, mist : νεφέλῃ εἰλυμένος ὤμους Il. 5.186. Cf. Il. 5.345, Il. 14.350, Il. 15.308, Il. 17.551, Il. 20.150 : Od. 8.562, Od. 11.15. Fig. : ν. μιν ἀμφεκάλυψεν (the mist of death) Il. 20.417. Cf. Il. 17.591 = Il. 18.22 : = Od. 24.315.

nifa/s.head: νιφάς
nifa/s.html: νιφάς -άδος, ἡ [νίφω.] Dat. pl. νιφάδεσσι Il. 3.222. 1 A snowflake G 222, Il. 12.156, Il. 19.357. So νιφάδες χιόνος Il. 12.278. 2 Snow : ν. ἠὲ χάλαζα Il. 15.170.

nomeu/s.head: νομεύς
nomeu/s.html: νομεύς ὁ [νου-, νεμ-, νέμω.] A herdsman or shepherd Il. 11.697, Il. 15.632, Il. 18.525, 577, 583 : Od. 4.413, Od. 16.3, 27, Od. 17.214= Od. 20.175, Od. 17.246, Od. 21.19. Joined with ἄνδρες Il. 17.65.

neou/tatos.head: νεούτατος
neou/tatos.html: νεούτατος -ον [νέος + οὐτάω.] Newly wounded, just wounded : χειρός Il. 13.539. Cf. Il. 18.536.

no/qos.head: νόθος
no/qos.html: νόθος -η. Not born in wedlock, bastard, illegitimate Il. 2.727, Il. 4.499, Il. 5.70, Il. 8.284, Il. 11.102, 490, Il. 13.173, 694 = Il. 15.333, Il. 16.738. Absol., a bastard : ὁ νόθος ἡνιόχευεν Il. 11.103.

nebro/s.head: νεβρός
nebro/s.html: νεβρός ὁ, ἡ. The young of the deer, a fawn Il. 4.243, Il. 8.248, 249, Il. 15.579, Il. 21.29, Il. 22.1, 189 : Od. 4.336 = Od. 17.127, Od. 19.230.

nekta/reos.head: νεκτάρεος
nekta/reos.html: νεκτάρεος [νέκταρ.] App., fragrant. Epithet of garments Il. 3.385, Il. 18.25.

nhsai/h.head: Νησαίη
nhsai/h.html: Νησαίη A Nereid Il. 18.40 .

neoardh/s.head: νεοαρδής
neoardh/s.html: νεοαρδής [νέος + ἄρδω, to water. Cf. ἀρδμός.] Newly watered : ἀλωήν Il. 21.346.

neo/ths.head: νεότης
neo/ths.html: νεότης -ητος, ἡ [νέος.] 1 Youth Il. 14.86. 2 Youthful vigour : ἀτέμβονται νεότητος Il. 23.445.

nemeshto/s.head: νεμεσητός
nemeshto/s.html: νεμεσητός νεμεσσητός [νεμεσάω.] 1 Absol. in neut. sing. νεμεσσητόν, something worthy of indignation or blame, a shame or disgrace : ν. κεν εἴη Il. 3.410, Il. 14.336 : Od. 22.489. With infin. : κεχολῶσθαι Il. 9.523. Cf. Il. 19.182, Il. 24.463 : Od. 22.59. 2 App., capable of or inclined to anger, easily roused to wrath (for the form cf. ἐπιεικτός) : νεμεσητός [ἐστιν] ὅμε προέηκεν Il. 11.649.

na/sths.head: Νάστης
na/sths.html: Νάστης (ἀγλαός). Son of Nomion and a leader of the Carians Il. 2.867, 870, 871.

nomi/wn.head: Νομίων
nomi/wn.html: Νομίων Father of Nastes and Amphimachus-2 Il. 2.871.

neusta/zw.head: νευστάζω
neusta/zw.html: νευστάζω [frequentative fr. νεύω.] 1 To make a quick inclination (with the head), nod Od. 18.154. Of one sitting in a state of helplessness: νευστάζων κεφαλῇ (letting his head drop forwards) Od. 18.240. Sim. of the accommodation of a helmet to the wearer's motion : νευστάζων κόρυθι Il. 20.162. 2 To convey an order by a motion of the head : ὀφρύσι νευστάζων (with my brows, bending the head forward) Od. 12.194.

ne/hlus.head: νέηλυς
ne/hlus.html: νέηλυς -υσος [νέος + ἐλὑθ'-, ἔρχομαι.] Newly come, a new-comer Il. 10.434, 558.

nhpu/tios.head: νηπύτιος
nhpu/tios.html: νηπύτιος [νη- + ἠπύω. Cf. L. infans.] Childish, foolish, senseless. In voc. νηπύτιε Il. 21.410, 441, 474, 585. In reference to speech : ἐπέεσσι νηπυτίοισιν Il. 20.211. Absol., a fool : νηπύτιοι ὥς Il. 13.292 = Il. 20.244. Cf. Il. 20.200, 431.

ni/suros.head: Νίσυρος
ni/suros.html: Νίσυρος An Aegean island, one of the Sporades Il. 2.676.

ni/fw.head: νίφω
ni/fw.html: νίφω [cf. L. niv-, nix, Eng. snow.] To snow Il. 12.280.

nh/ios.head: νήϊος
nh/ios.html: νήϊος [νηῦς.] Of or for a ship : δόρυ Il. 15.410, Il. 17.744 : Od. 9.384. Cf. Od. 9.498. Absol. in neut. νήϊον, a piece of ship-timber Il. 3.62, Il. 13.391 = Il. 16.484.

nai/w.head: ναίω1
nai/w.html:
ναίω1 [νασ-.] 3 sing. pa. iterative nai/eske Il. 5.708, Il. 16.719. 3 pl. -ον Il. 2.758. Aor. νάσσα Od. 4.174. 3 sing. aor. pass. νάσθη Il. 14.119. (ἀπο-) 1 To live, dwell, abide, have one's home : ἔναιεν ἐνὶ φηρῇ Il. 5.543. Cf. Il. 2.130, Il. 6.13, Il. 9.154, Il. 13.176, Il. 16.233, etc. : Od. 3.292, Od. 4.98, Od. 5.58, Od. 13.240, Od. 15.96, etc. 2 Of a house, by a sort of personification, to stand, be situated : δόμον δείξω, ἐπεί μοι πατρὸς ἐγγύθι ναίει Od. 7.29. So of islands, to lie : νήσων, αἳ ναίουσι πέρην ἁλός Il. 2.626. 3 To live in, dwell in, have one's home in, inhabit, hold, have : Ἀσπληδόνα Il. 2.511. Cf. Il. 2.593, Il. 3.74, Il. 6.15, Il. 9.484, Il. 15.190, etc. : Od. 1.51, Od. 4.555, Od. 9.36, 49, 113, etc. 4 In pres. pple. pass. with εὖ, of places, well inhabited, holding a goodly people : εὖ ναιόμενον πτολίεθρον Il. 1.164, Il. 2.133, Il. 9.402, Il. 13.380. Cf. Il. 3.400, Il. 5.489, Il. 9.149, 291, Il. 13.815, Il. 14.255 = Il. 15.28, Il. 16.572: Od. 13.285. 5 In aor., to establish or settle (a city) : Ἄργεΐ κέ οἱ νάσσα πόλιν Od. 4.174. 6 In aor. pass. in mid. sense, to establish oneself, settle, take up one's abode : Ἄργεϊ νάσθη Il. 14.119.
ναίω2 [= νάω.] To flow, be filled to overflowing : ναῖον ὀρῷ ἄγγεα Od. 9.222.

no/os.head: νόος
no/os.html: νόος -ου, ὁ. Contr. νοῦς Od. 10.240. 1 The mind : μὴ κεῦθε νόῳ Il. 1.363, ν. ἔμπεδος ἦεν Il. 11.813. Cf. Il. 1.132, Il. 9.514, Il. 10.122, Il. 12.255, Il. 15.52, etc. : Od. 1.347, Od. 2.92, Od. 7.263, Od. 13.255, Od. 20.366, etc. 2 Mental power or reach, intelligence : περὶ νόον ἐστὶ βροτῶν (in . . .) Od. 1.66. Cf. Il. 10.226, Il. 13.732, Il. 15.643, Il. 18.419 : Od. 10.494. 3 Sense, good sense, judgment, discretion : ν. ἀπόλωλε καὶ αἰδώς Il. 15.129. Cf. Il. 10.391, Il. 20.133 : Od. 6.320, Od. 7.73. 4 One's mind, spirit, nature, disposition : σοὶ ἀτάρβητος ν. ἐστίν Il. 3.63. Cf. Il. 16.35, Il. 23.484 : Od. 1.3, Od. 5.190, Od. 6.121= Od. 9.176= Od. 13.202, Od. 8.576, Od. 18.136, 332 = 392, Od. 18.381. 5 One's mind, will, liking : ὅπῃ τοι ν. ἔπλετο Il. 22.185. Cf. Il. 9.108 (not by my good will), Il. 20.25. 6 What one has in his mind, his mind, purpose, design, intent, what he has in view : ὄφρα κʼ ἔτι γνῶμεν Τρώων νόον Il. 22.382. Cf. Il. 2.192, Il. 7.447, Il. 8.143 : Od. 2.124, 281, Od. 4.256, Od. 5.103, 137, Od. 11.177, Od. 13.229, Od. 21.205, Od. 22.215. 7 A plan, design, device, a scheme, system or method of action : τόνδε νόον ἔχοντες Il. 4.309. Cf. Il. 9.104, Il. 15.509, Il. 24.367 : νόον σχέθε τόνδʼ ἐνὶ θυμῷ Od. 14.490. Cf. Od. 5.23= Od. 24.479. 8 Counsel, concerting of measures, contriving, planning, scheming : νόῳ καὶ ἐπίφρονι βουλῇ Od. 3.128. Cf. Il. 14.62 : Od. 4.267, Od. 12.211, Od. 13.305, Od. 16.197, 374, Od. 19.326. 9 What one has in his mind, his expectation, hope, desire : τοῖσιν ὅδʼ ἦν ν. Il. 15.699. Cf. Il. 23.149. 10 What one has in his mind, what he knows or can tell : δαῆναι ἐμὸν νόον Od. 4.493.

nhkouste/w.head: νηκουστέω
nhkouste/w.html: νηκουστέω [νη- + ἀκούω.] To neglect the behest or summons of. With genit. : θεᾶς Il. 20.14.

ne/stwr.head: Νέστωρ
ne/stwr.html: Νέστωρ (ἀντίθεος, γέρων, Γερήνιος, δῖος, ἡδυεπής, ίππηλάτα, ἱππόδαμος, ἱππότα, λιγὺς Πυλίων ἀγορητής, μεγάθυμος , μέγα κῦδος Ἀχαιῶν, μέγας , οὖρος Ἀχαιῶν, ποιμὴν λαῶν , Πυλοιγενὴς βασιλεύς, ὑπέρθυμος). Patronymic Νηλεΐδης, Νηληϊάδης. King of Pylus, son of Neleus, husband of Eurydice and father of Antilochus, Peisistratus, Echephron, Stratius, Perseus-2, Aretus-2 and Thrasymedes. Had reigned already over two generations Il. 1.247; intervenes in the quarrel between Achilles and Agamemnon Il. 1.254 ; Oneirus appears to Ag. in his form Il. 2.21; he addresses the βουλή Il. 2.77; visited by Ag. in his inspection Il. 4.293; reproaches the Greeks, no champion coming forward against Hector, and tells the tale of the fighting between the Pylians and the Arcadians Il. 7.123; advises the burning of the dead and the building of the wall Il. 7.325; is cut off in the fight Il. 8.80, but is rescued by Diomedes 99; advises the setting of a guard Il. 9.52; advises the restoration of Briseis with gifts Il. 9.94, advises the sending of the embassy 162; is wakened by Ag. Il. 10.73, visits the guard 180; carries off the wounded Machaon Il. 11.516; his appeal in his hut to Patroclus and his tale of the fighting between the Pylians and the Epeians Il. 11.655; encounters the wounded chiefs Il. 14.27; his advice to Antilochus before the chariot-race Il. 23.306, is presented by Achilles with a remaining prize 615; etc. : hospitably receives Telemachus at Pylus Od. 3.31, tells, him the tale of his return 102, advises him to go to Menelaus 317, dispatches him 474; restrained the flight of the Greeks when Thetis appeared to take part in the funeral rites of Achilles Od. 24.50; etc.

nuo/s.head: νυός
nuo/s.html: νυός -οῦ, ἡ. A daughter-in-law : νυὸν ἀνδρῶν αἰχμητάων (Helen being regarded as having contracted affinity with her husband's nation) Il. 3.49, θυγατέρες ἰδὲ νυοί Il. 24.166. Cf. Il. 22.65 : Od. 3.451.

neoi/h.head: νεοίη
neoi/h.html: νεοίη ἡ [obscurely formed fr. νέος.] App., the fire or impulsiveness of youth Il. 23.604.

no/stos.head: νόστος
no/stos.html: νόστος -ου, ὁ [cf. νέομαι.] 1 A coming to or reaching a specified place, a getting to it : νέων ἐπιμαίεο νόστου γαίης Φαιήκων (to the land of the . . .) Od. 5.344. 2 A returning or going back : νῆας ἔπι Il. 10.509. Cf. Il. 9.622. 3 A going home, one's return home or home-coming, one's journey home Od. 1.326, Od. 3.132, 142, Od. 4.497, Od. 5.108, Od. 9.37, 97, 102, Od. 10.15, Od. 11.110= Od. 12.137, Od. 11.384, Od. 15.3, Od. 18.242, Od. 23.351, etc. Implying more or less a happy or safe return Il. 2.155, 251, Il. 9.413, 434, Il. 16.82 : Od. 1.5, 13, 77, 94 (to seek for tidings of his homeward bound father), 287 (learn that he has so far safely accomplished the homeward journey), Od. 3.160, Od. 4.519, Od. 6.14, Od. 12.419, Od. 14.61, Od. 22.323, etc.

numfi/os.head: νυμφίος
numfi/os.html: νυμφίος [νύμφη.] Not long married : παιδὸς νυμφίον Il. 23.223. Cf. Od. 7.65.

ni/zw.head: νίζω
ni/zw.html: νίζω Fut. νίψω Od. 19.376. 3 sing. νίψει Od. 19.356. 3 sing. aor. ἔνιψε Il. 16.229. νίψε Il. 10.575 : Od. 19.505. Aor. νίψον Od. 19.358. 3 sing. aor. mid. νίψατο Il. 16.230. Pple. νιψάμενος Il. 24.305 : Od. 2.261, Od. 12.336. Pl. νιψάμενοι Od. 10.182. Infin. νίψασθαι Od. 1.138, Od. 4.54, Od. 7.174, Od. 10.370, Od. 15.137, Od. 17.93. 3 sing. pf. pass. νένιπται Il. 24.419. (ἀπο-, ἐξαπο-.) 1 To wash, cleanse: σπόγγοισι τραπέζας νίξον Od. 1.112. Cf. Il. 16.229. 2 To wash the feet of : νίψον σοῖο ἄνακτος ὁμήλικα Od. 19.358. Cf. Od. 19.374, 392, 505. With double acc. of person and part : ἥ σε πόδας νίψει Od. 19.356. Cf. Od. 19.376. 3 To wash away or off : ἐπεί σφιν κῦμα θαλάσσης ἱδρῶ νίψεν ἀπὸ χρωτός Il. 10.575. Cf. Il. 11.830, 846, Il. 24.419. With ἀπό, off: ὕδατι νίζοντες ἄπο βρότον Il. 7.425. 4 In mid., to wash (one's hands) : νίψατο αὐτὸς χεῖρας Il. 16.230 : χεῖρας νιψάμενος ἁλός (genit. of material, in the . . . ) Od. 2.261. Cf. Od. 10.182, Od. 12.336. To wash (one's body). With second acc. of what is washed away or off : χρόα νίζετο ἅλμην Od. 6.224. To wash one's hands: νιψάμενος κύπελλον ἐδέξατο Il. 24.305. Cf. Od. 1.138 = Od. 4.54 = Od. 7.174 = Od. 10.370 = Od. 15.137 = Od. 17.93.

nhpiaxeu/w.head: νηπιαχεύω
nhpiaxeu/w.html: νηπιαχεύω [νηπίαχος.] Of a child, to sport or play : ὅτε παύσαιτο νηπιαχεύων Il. 22.502.

nemesi/zomai.head: νεμεσίζομαι
nemesi/zomai.html: νεμεσίζομαι [νέμεσις.] 1 = νεμεσάω 1 Il. 5.872. With the cause expressed by acc. and infin.: οὐ νεμεσίζομʼ Ἀχαιοὺς ἀσχαλάαν (I cannot blame them) Il. 2.296. With dat. : Ἥρῃ Il. 8.407, 421. Cf. Od. 2.239. With dat. and the cause expressed by an acc. : οὐ νεμεσίζῃ Ἄρῃ τάδε ἔργα; Il. 5.757. 2 = νεμεσάω 3 : ὑμέτερος εἰ θυμὸς νεμεσίζεται αὐτῶν (if you can see your conduct in its true light) Od. 2.138. Sim. with infin.: νεμεσιζέσθω Πάτροκλον κυσὶν μέλπηθρα γενέσθαι (let the thought sting him) Il. 17.254. 3 To fear the wrath of, stand in awe of, reverence : θεούς Od. 1.263.

nei/aira.head: νείαιρα
nei/aira.html: νείαιρα -ης [comp. Cf. νέατος, νείατος.] The lower part of : νειαίρῃ ἐν γαστρί Il. 5.539 = Il. 17.519, Il. 5.616. Cf. Il. 16.465.

nh=sos.head: νῆσος
nh=sos.html: νῆσος -ου, ἡ. An island : Ἐχινάων ἱεράων νήσων Il. 2.626. Cf. Il. 2.108, 677, 721, Il. 3.445, Il. 18.208, Il. 21.454, Il. 22.45 : εἶδον νῆσον (that it was an island on which I was) Od. 10.195. Cf. Od. 1.50, Od. 3.171, Od. 4.368, Od. 5.13, Od. 9.130, Od. 10.3, Od. 12.143, Od. 13.95, etc.

nio/bh.head: Νιόβη
nio/bh.html: Νιόβη (ἠΰκομος). Her children slain by Apollo and Artemis and she herself turned to stone on Mt. Sipylus Il. 24.602, 606 .

nu/c.head: νύξ
nu/c.html: νύξ νυκτός, ἡ [cf. L. nox, Eng. night.] 1 Night, the night, the period of darkness : ἐπήλυθε ν. Il. 8.488. Cf. Il. 1.47, Il. 2.57, Il. 3.11, Il. 7.282, Il. 14.78, Il. 24.366, etc. : νύκτα διὰ δνοφερήν Od. 15.50. Cf. Od. 4.429, Od. 5.294, Od. 9.143, Od. 10.86, Od. 19.66, Od. 23.243, etc. 2 A night considered as a space of time : πολλὰς ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον Il. 9.325. Cf. Il. 5.490, Il. 8.529, Il. 9.470, Il. 10.188, 251, 252, 312 = 399, Il. 18.274, 340, Il. 22.432, Il. 23.186, Il. 24.73, 745 : Od. 2.105, 345, Od. 3.151, Od. 5.466, Od. 12.312, Od. 17.515, Od. 19.340, Od. 20.85, Od. 22.195, etc. 3 A night considered as a point or unit of time or as one of a series : δεκάτη ν. Il. 9.474. Cf. Il. 9.78, Il. 10.497, Il. 18.251, Il. 22.102 : τῇδε νυκτί Od. 20.88. Cf. Od. 7.253 = Od. 14.314, Od. 12.447, Od. 14.93, Od. 18.272. 4 Night personified Il. 14.259, 261. 5 Darkness, a pall or cloud of darkness : Ζεὺς ἐπὶ νύκτα τάνυσεν ὑσμίνῃ Il. 16.567. Cf. Il. 5.23, 506 : Od. 11.19, Od. 20.351, 362, Od. 23.372. The darkness of death or of stupor : ὄσσε ν. ἐκάλυψεν Il. 5.310= Il. 11.356. Cf. Il. 5.659= Il. 13.580, Il. 13.425, Il. 14.439, Il. 22.466.

nemesa/w.head: νεμεσάω
nemesa/w.html: νεμεσάω νεμεσσάω [νέμεσις.] 1 To be righteously indignant or vexed, to conceive, feel or express blame or censure, utter reproach Il. 4.507, Il. 8.198, Il. 10.145 = Il. 16.22, Il. 13.293 : Od. 17.481 = Od. 21.285. With dat.: ἄλλῃ νεμεσῶ Od. 6.286. Cf. Il. 13.16 = 353, Il. 23.494 : Od. 2.101 = Od. 19.146 = Od. 24.136, Od. 21.147. With dat. and with the cause expressed by a pple. : οὐ νεμεσῶ Ἀγαμέμνονι ὀτρύνοντι μάχεσθαι Il. 4.413. By an acc. : μή μοι τόδε νεμέσσα, οὕνεκα . . . Od. 23.213. By an infin.: μή μοι νεμεσήσετε τείσασθαι . . . Il. 15.115. 2 So in mid. and in aor. pass. in mid. sense : πᾶσι νεμεσσηθεῖσα μετηύδα (her feelings getting the better of her) Il. 15.103, νεμεσσηθείς χʼ ὑποείξω (though indignant, repressing my indignation) 211. Cf. Il. 15.227 : νεμεσσῶμαι δέ τʼ ἀκούων Od. 21.169. Cf. Od. 1.228, Od. 19.264. The cause expressed by an acc. : ὃς νεμεσσᾶται κακὰ ἔργα Od. 14.284. By acc. and infin.: νεμεσσήθη ξεῖνον δηθὰ θύρῃσιν ἐφεστάμεν Od. 1.119. Cf. Od. 18.227. By infin. alone : νεμεσσῶμαί γʼ οὐδὲν κλαίειν . . . (I say nothing against it) Od. 4.195. With dat. : τῷ νεμέσσηθεν Il. 2.223. Cf. Il. 10.115, 129, Il. 13.119, Il. 17.93, 100, Il. 24.53 : Od. 1.158, Od. 15.69, Od. 19.121. 3 In sim. forms, to be dissatisfied or displeased with oneself : νεμεσσήθητε θυμῷ (think shame (to stand idle)) Il. 16.544. Cf. Od. 2.64. With infin. Od. 4.158.

nhpie/h.head: νηπιέη
nhpie/h.html: νηπιέη -ης, ἡ [νήπιος.] 1 Childishness, childish ways : ἐν νηπιέῃ Il. 9.491. In pl. : ἐπεὶ ποιήσῃ ἀθύρματα νηπιέῃσιν Il. 15.363. 2 Folly, thoughtlessness. In pl. : νηπιέῃσι ποδῶν ἀρετὴν ἀναφαίνων Il. 20.411. Foolish or thoughtless action. In pl. : τοῖσιν εὐπείθης ἡγήσατο νηπιέῃσιν Od. 24.469.

ne/mos.head: νέμος
ne/mos.html: νέμος τό. A glade or dell Il. 11.480.

nwi/teros.head: νωΐτερος
nwi/teros.html: νωΐτερος -η, -ον [νῶϊ.] Our (of two persons) : λέχος Il. 15.39 : ὄπα Od. 12.185.

ni/ssomai.head: νίσσομαι
ni/ssomai.html: νίσσομαι νίσομαι [for νι-νσ-ομαι, redup. fr. νς- νεσ-, conn. with νέομαι.] (μετα-, ποτι-.) 1 To go or come back, return : ἐκ πεδίου νίσοντο Il. 12.119. Cf. Od. 4.701 = Od. 5.19. 2 To take one's way go, come : πόλεμόνδε Il. 13.186, Il. 15.577. Cf. Il. 18.566. 3 In pres. with fut. sense, to go or come back, return : οὐ γάρ ἔτʼ αὖτις νίσομαι ἐξ Ἀΐδαο Il. 23.76. Cf. Od. 10.42.

ne/w.head: νέω1
ne/w.html:
νέω1 [σνυ-.] 3 pl. impf. ἔννεον (ἔσνεϝον) Il. 21.11. To swim : χείρεσσι νέων Od. 5.344. Cf. Il. 21.11 : Od. 5.442.
νέω2 (ἐπι-) To spin. In mid. Od. 7.198.

ne/omai.head: νέομαι
ne/omai.html: νέομαι [conn. with νόστος.] Contr. νεῦμαι Il. 18.136. 2 sing. νεῖαι (νέεαι) Od. 11.114, Od. 12.141. (ἀν-, ἀπο-) 1 To go or come back or home, return : σαώτερος ὥς κε νέηαι Il. 1.32, ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν Il. 2.453. Cf. Il. 2.236, Il. 3.74, Il. 5.907, Il. 9.42, Il. 18.377, etc. : Od. 1.17, 87, Od. 3.60, Od. 4.351, Od. 9.95, Od. 12.334, Od. 15.3, Od. 23.23, etc. 2 To take one's way, proceed upon one's way, proceed, go, come, depart : βουλῆς ἐξ Il. 2.84. Cf. Il. 18.240, Il. 20.6, Il. 21.48, 598, Il. 23.51, 662: ταῦτα τελευτήσας νεόμην Od. 4.585, Od. 17.148. Cf. Od. 2.52, Od. 3.170, Od. 4.8, Od. 12.188, Od. 13.30, 206, Od. 14.261 = Od. 17.430, Od. 14.498, Od. 15.72, Od. 18.186 = Od. 22.434 = 496, Od. 21.374, Od. 22.484. Of rivers, to take their way, run, flow Il. 12.32. 3 In pres. with fut. sense, to go or come back or home, return : ἐπεὶ οὐ νέομαί γʼ φίλην ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν Il. 18.101 = Il. 23.150. Cf. Il. 3.257. Il. 14.221, Il. 17.497, Il. 18.136, Il. 19.330 : Od. 2.238, Od. 4.633, Od. 6.110, Od. 11.114 = Od. 12.141, Od. 11.176, Od. 14.152, Od. 20.156, Od. 24.460. To take one's way, go, depart : αὐτὰρ ἐγὼ νέομαι Od. 13.61.

nesto/reos.head: Νεστόρεος
nesto/reos.html: Νεστόρεος Adj. from Νέστωρ 54, Il. 8.113, 192.

nw=roy.head: νῶροψ
nw=roy.html: νῶροψ -οπος. App., gleaming, glancing, or the like. Epithet of χαλκός Il. 2.578, Il. 7.206, Il. 11.16, Il. 13.406, Il. 16.130, Il. 14.383 := Od. 24.467 = 500.

nhdu/s.head: νηδύς
nhdu/s.html: νηδύς -ύος, ἡ. The belly Il. 13.290, Il. 20.486 : Od. 9.296. The womb Il. 24.496.

nwqh/s.head: νωθής
nwqh/s.html: νωθής Obstinately lazy, refractory Il. 11.559.

nwma/w.head: νωμάω
nwma/w.html: νωμάω [νέμω.] 1 To distribute or give out among a company : σπλάγχνα Od. 20.252. Without expressed object Il. 1.471= Il. 9.176 := Od. 3.340 = Od. 21.272, Od. 7.183, Od. 13.54= Od. 18.425. 2 To handle, wield, move, control : σκῆπτρον Il. 3.218. Cf. Il. 5.594, Il. 7.238, Il. 15.677 : Od. 10.32, Od. 12.218, Od. 21.245, 393, 400, Od. 22.10. To put in motion, ply (the limbs, etc.) : γούνατʼ ἐνώμα Il. 10.358, Il. 22.144. Cf. Il. 15.269, Il. 22.24. In reference to the mind, to apply it (skilfully) to the matter in hand, have it in (constant) practice or readiness : νόον πολυκερδέα νωμῶν Od. 13.255. Sim. in reference to the contents of the mind : κέρδεʼ ἐνώμας Od. 18.216. Cf. Od. 20.257.

nh/nemos.head: νήνεμος
nh/nemos.html: νήνεμος -ον [νη- + ἄνεμος.] Windless : ὅτε τʼ ἔπλετο νήνεμος αἰθήρ Il. 8.556.

no/hma.head: νόημα
no/hma.html: νόημα -ατος, τό [νοέω.] 1 A thought, idea, notion: τίπτε τοι ἐνὶ φρεσὶ τοῦτο ν. ἔπλετο; Od. 2.363. Cf. Il. 7.456, Il. 18.295 : Od. 7.36, Od. 15.326, Od. 17.403. 2 The mind : οὐκέτι τοι φρένες ἔμπεδοί [εἰσιν] οὐδὲ ν. Od. 18.215. Cf. Od. 18.220, Od. 20.82, 326. 3 Mental power or reach, intelligence : σεῖό κε νοήματι προβαλοίμην (in . . . ) Il. 19.218. 4 One's mind, nature, disposition : αἰεί τοι τοιοῦτον ἐνὶ στήθεσσι ν. Od. 13.330. Cf. Il. 24.40 : Od. 6.183. 5 What one has in one's mind, a purpose, design, intention : οὐχ Ἕκτορι πάντα νοήματʼ ἐκτελέει Il. 10.104. Cf. Il. 18.328 : Od. 8.559, Od. 23.30. In collective sense : Διὸς νόημα (his purposes) Il. 17.409. 6 A device or contrivance : νοήμασι κερδαλέοισιν Od. 8.548. Cf. Od. 2.121. 7 What comes into one's mind or occurs to one : οὔ τι νοήματος ἤμβροτεν ἐσθλοῦ (the right thing to do) Od. 7.292. Cf. Od. 14.273.

neu/w.head: νεύω
neu/w.html: νεύω (ἀνα-, ἐπι-, κατα-) 1 To make a quick inclination of the head, bend the head : ψαῦον κόρυθες νευόντων (genit. with κόρυθες, as the men bent their heads) Il. 13.133 = Il. 16.217. Of the nodding of the crest of a helmet Il. 6.470, Il. 3.337 = Il. 11.42 = Il. 15.481 = Il. 16.138 : = Od. 22.124. To bend (the head). Of persons on whom destruction has come : νεύοιεν κεφαλάς δεδμημένοι Od. 18.237. 2 To nod in token or sanction of a promise, promise, undertake, vouchsafe : ἐπʼ ὀφρύσι νεῦσεν (with his brows, bending the head forward) Il. 1.528 = Il. 17.209. With infin. : νεῦσέ οἱ λαὸον ἔμμεναι Il. 8.246. 3 To convey an order or make a sign by a motion of the head : νεῦσʼ αἴας φοίνικι Il. 9.223 : ἐπʼ ὀφρύσι νεῦσεν Od. 16.164. Cf. Od. 16.283, Od. 17.330, Od. 21.431. With infin.: στορέσαι λέχος Il. 9.620. With ἀνά, to make a sign in prohibition (cf. ἀνανεύω 3): ἀνὰ δʼ ὀφρύσι νεῦον Od. 9.468.

ne/mw.head: νέμω
ne/mw.html: νέμω 3 sing. aor. ἔνειμε Od. 14.449. νεῖμε Il. 9.217, Il. 24.626 : Od. 14.436, Od. 20.253. 3 pl. ἔνειμαν Od. 14.210. νεῖμαν Il. 3.274. Imp. νεῖμον Od. 7.179, Od. 13.50. (ἀμφι-, ἐπι-.) 1 To give as one's lot or portion, assign : οἰκία Od. 14.210. In reference to one's fortune : Ζεὺς αὐτὸς νέμει ὄλβον Od. 6.188. To distribute or give out among a company : κρέα Il. 9.217 = Il. 24.626. Cf. Od. 7.179 = Od. 13.50, Od. 8.470, Od. 10.357, Od. 14.436, 449, Od. 15.140, Od. 20.253. Without expressed object : κήρυκες νεῖμαν ἀρίστοις Il. 3.274. 2 In mid., to get as one's lot or portion, to hold, occupy, possess, enjoy (places, lands, etc.) : τέμενος νεμόμεσθα Il. 12.313. Cf. Il. 2.496, 504, 531, Il. 6.195, Il. 20.8, etc. : οἳ νεμόμεσθʼ Ἰθάκην Od. 2.167. Cf. Od. 7.26, Od. 11.185, Od. 20.336. To have one's abode, dwell, be settled : ἀμφʼ Ἅρμʼ ἐνέμοντο Il. 2.499. 3 To drive one's flock : ἐπῆλθε νέμων Od. 9.233. 4 In mid., of domestic animals, to feed, crop the herbage, graze : σύες νέμονται πὰρ κόρακος πέτρῃ Od. 13.407. Cf. Il. 15.631 : Od. 20.164. To feed on, crop, graze : νέμεαι ἄνθεα ποίης Od. 9.449. Cf. Il. 5.777. Of fire : πυρὸς μένος ἧκε, ὄφρα νέμοιτο (might consume the corpses) Il. 23.177. In pass. of something consumed by fire : ὡς εἴ τε πυρὶ χθὼν νέμοιτο Il. 2.780.

ni/kh.head: νίκη
ni/kh.html: νίκη -ης, ἡ. 1 Victory, the upper hand, in fight or in a contest Il. 3.457, Il. 4.13, Il. 6.339, Od. 8.176, Il. 13.166 (the victory which had eluded his grasp), Il. 14.364, Il. 16.689, etc. : Od. 22.236. 2 In gen., victory, getting the better of someone Od. 11.544.

no/sfi.head: νόσφι
no/sfi.html: νόσφι I adv. 1 Away, far away : ν. ἐόντες Od. 3.193. At a distance, away, absent : ὅτε σὺ ν. γένηαι Od. 10.486. Cf. Il. 22.332 : Od. 14.147, 527. 2 Apart, aloof, by himself or themselves : ν. καθήμεναι Il. 4.9. Cf. Il. 5.322, Il. 10.416, Il. 15.244, Il. 17.382, 408 : Od. 11.544. 3 Away, off, to a distance, apart, aloof : ν. κιόντα Il. 11.284, Il. 14.440. Cf. Il. 11.80, Il. 24.583 : Od. 4.289, Od. 8.286, Od. 13.164. In reference to direction, away, aloof : ν. ἰδών Od. 17.304. Cf. Il. 13.4. II Prep. with genit. 1 Far from : ν. φίλων πάντων Il. 14.256. Cf. Il. 19.422, Il. 22.508. In the absence of : οὓς ἐπέφνετε ν. ἐμεῖο Il. 21.135. 2 Apart or aloof from, at a distance from : ν. πόληος Od. 1.185 = Od. 24.308, Od. 16.383, Od. 24.212. Cf. Il. 6.443, Il. 18.465 : Od. 4.367. Apart from, having separated oneself from or left : ὅτε τʼ ἤλυθε ν. Ἀχαιῶν Il. 5.803. Without reference to place : τοί κεν Ἀχαιῶν ν. βουλεύωσιν Il. 2.347. 3 Away from, to a distance from : ἑτάρων ν. λιασθείς Il. 1.349. Cf. Il. 8.490, Il. 23.365. 4 Apart from, without the help or countenance of : πολλὰ πονήσατο νόσφιν ἐμεῖο Il. 9.348. Cf. Od. 14.9 = 451. 5 Apart from, except : ν. θεῶν Il. 12.466. Cf. Il. 20.7 : Od. 1.20.

nh=is.head: νῆις
nh=is.html: νῆις -ιδος [νη- + (ϝ)ιδ-, εἴδω.] Lacking knowledge, unskilled Il. 7.198. Lacking knowledge of, unskilled in. With genit.: ἀέθλων Od. 8.179.

nhkerdh/s.head: νηκερδής
nhkerdh/s.html: νηκερδής -ές [νη- + κέρδος.] That brings no gain or profit, profitless : βουλήν Il. 17.469 : ἔπος Od. 14.509.

nei=kos.head: νεῖκος
nei=kos.html: νεῖκος τό. 1 A quarrel, contention, dispute: τοῦ εἵνεκα ν. ὄρωρεν Il. 3.87 = Il. 7.374 = 388. Cf. Il. 2.376, Il. 4.37, Il. 14.205 = 304, Il. 18.497, Il. 22.116, Il. 24.107 : Od. 7.74, Od. 8.75, Od. 12.440. Contention, strife : ν. ἄριστε (in . . . ) Il. 23.483. Cf. Od. 20.267, Od. 21.303. 2 The strife of war, lust of battle : ν. σφʼ ὁμοίϊον ἔμβαλε μέσσῳ Il. 4.444. A fight or battle : ὣς ἄγε ν. Ἀθήνη Il. 11.721. Cf. Il. 11.671, 737, Il. 13.122, 271, 333, Il. 15.400, Il. 17.544 : Od. 16.98 = 116, Od. 18.264. Fighting, battle : πόνος καὶ ν. Il. 12.348, ἔριδος μέγα ν. (battle-strife) Il. 17.384. Cf. Il. 12.361, Il. 20.140, Il. 21.513 : Od. 24.543. The tide of battle, the battle: ν. ἀπωσαμένους Il. 12.276. 3 A reproach, a reviling or abusing : φεύγων νείκεα πατρός Il. 9.448. Cf. Il. 20.251. Reproach: νείκει ὀνειδίζων (in . . . ) Il. 7.95.

neo/teuktos.head: νεότευκτος
neo/teuktos.html: νεότευκτος [νέος + τευκ-, τεύχω.] Newly wrought : κασσιτέροιο Il. 21.592.

nwleme/s.head: νωλεμές
nwleme/s.html: νωλεμές (cf. next). Without cease, cessation, pause, relaxation of effort, blenching : μάχην ἔχουσιν Il. 14.58. Cf. Il. 17.413. Strengthened by αἰεί Il. 9.317= Il. 17.148, Il. 17.385, Il. 19.232 : Od. 16.191, Od. 22.228.

neurh/.head: νευρή
neurh/.html: νευρή -ῆς ἡ [cf. νεῦρον.] Locative νευρῆφι Od. 11.607. This form as ablative Il. 8.300, 309, Il. 13.585, Il. 15.313, Il. 16.773, Il. 21.113. A bowstring Il. 4.118, 123, 125, Il. 8.300, 309, 324, 328, Il. 11.476, 664, Il. 13.585, Il. 15.313. 463, 469, Il. 16.773, Il. 21.113 : Od. 11.607, Od. 19.587, Od. 21.97 = 127, 410, 419, Od. 24.171.

noh/mwn.head: νοήμων
noh/mwn.html:
νοήμων -ονος [νοέω.] Right-thinking : οὔ (τι) νοήμονες οὐδὲ δίκαιοι Od. 2.282, Od. 3.133, Od. 13.209.
Νοήμων-1 Trojan. killed by Odysseus Il. 5.678.
Νοήμων-2 A comrade of Antilochus Il. 23.612.
Νοήμων-3 (φαίδιμος). An Ithacan, son of Phronius. Lent Telemachus a ship Od. 2.386, Od. 4.630, 648.

narka/w.head: ναρκάω
narka/w.html: ναρκάω To become numbed or deadened : νάρκησε χείρ Il. 8.328.

noe/w.head: νοέω
noe/w.html: νοέω [νόος.] (εἰσ-, προ-) 1 To perceive with the eye, see, discern, mark, observe (often with complementary pple. or adj.) : τὸν ὡς ἐνόησεν ἐρχόμενον Il. 3.21, τῶν οὔ τινʼ ἰδέειν δύναμʼ οὐδέ νοῆσαι Il. 5.475. Cf. Il. 2.391, Il. 3.30, 396, Il. 4.200, Il. 5.95, Il. 6.470, Il. 12.143, Il. 15.348, Il. 21.49, etc. : Od. 1.58, Od. 4.116, 653, Od. 6.163, Od. 8.271, Od. 12.28, Od. 16.5, Od. 19.232, etc. Absol. Il. 3.374, Il. 5.669, Od. 8.91, Il. 12.393, Il. 17.483, etc.: Od. 4.148, Od. 16.160, Od. 19.478, Od. 22.162, etc. 2 To perceive with themid, see, mark, undersatnd: οὔ τι δολοφροσύνην ἐνόησεν Il. 19.112. Cf. Il. 1.522 :Od. 6.67, Od. 18.228, Od. 20.309, 367. With dependent clause : τὸ νήπιος οὐκ ἐνόησεν, ὡς . . . Od. 9.442. Cf. Od. 22.32. Absol. Il. 10.225 : Od. 1.322, Od. 21.257. With dependent clause : νοῆσαι ὅππως . . . Il. 1.343. Cf. Il. 10.224, Il. 20.264, Il. 22.445. In pres. pple., not lacking perception, recognizing quickly the calls of expediency or propriety, intelligent, of good sense : καὶ αὐτῇ περ νοεούσῃ Il. 1.577. Cf. Il. 23.305 : Od. 16.136 = Od. 17.193 = 281. 3 To think of, propose to oneself, purpose : μή μοι ταῦτα νόει φρεσίν Il. 9.600. Cf. Il. 23.140 = 193 : Od. 2.382 = 393 = Od. 4.795 = Od. 14.112 = Od. 18.187, Od. 4.219, Od. 5.188, 382, Od. 14.251, Od. 16.409, Od. 17.576 (taken this into his head), Od. 23.242, 344. 4 To turn over in one's mind, think out, plan, contrive, devise : τοῦτό γʼ ἐναίσιμον οὐκ ἐνόησεν Od. 2.122, Od. 7.299. Cf. Il. 1.543, 549, Il. 7.358 = Il. 12.232, Il. 9.104, 105, Il. 23.415. Absol. : περίοιδε νοῆσαι Il. 10.247. Cf. Od. 5.170. 5 To think of, have the wit to say or do : ἄλλʼ αὐτὸς νοήσεις Od. 3.26. Cf. Od. 18.230. With complementary infin.: τό οὔ τις ἐνόησε, μηροῦ ἐξερύσαι δόρυ Il. 5.665. Followed directly by infin.: οὐκ ἐνόησα καταβῆναι ἰὼν ἐς κλίμακα Od. 11.62. In mid.: οὐ μάστιγα νοήσαθʼ ἑλέσθαι Il. 10.501. Absol.: ὅππως οἱ κατὰ μοῖραν ὑποκρίναιτο νοήσας (should hit upon the right interpretation) Od. 15.170. 6 To think of a thing, have it occur to one : ἤ λάθετʼ ἤ οὐκ ἐνόησεν Il. 9.537. 7 To think, with the thought directly reported Il. 15.81. 8 To be minded or disposed, have one's mind made up. With infin.: νοέω καί αὐτὸς Ἕκτορα λῦσαι Il. 24.560. Cf. Il. 22.235. 9 To consider the case of, make up one's mind as to : νόησον Αἰνείαν, ἢ . . . ἦ . . . Il. 20.310.

nauboli/dhs.head: Ναυβολίδης-1.
nauboli/dhs.html:
Ναυβολίδης-1. Patronymic of Iphitus-1 Il. 2.518.
Ναυβολίδης-2. Patronymic of Euryalus-2 Od. 8.116.

nou=sos.head: νοῦσος
nou=sos.html: νοῦσος -ου, ἡ. A disease, illness, ailment Il. 1.10, Il. 13.667, 670 : Od. 5.395, Od. 9.411, Od. 11.172, 200, Od. 15.408.

nosfi/zomai.head: νοσφίζομαι
nosfi/zomai.html: νοσφίζομαι [νόσφι.] Aor. νοσφισάμην Od. 19.339. 3 sing. νοσφίσατο Od. 11.425. Nom. sing. fem. pple. νοσφισσαμένη Od. 19.579, Od. 21.77, 104. Acc. νοσφισσαμένην Od. 4.263. Aor. pple. in pass. form νοσφισθείς Od. 11.73. 1 To turn away in incredulousness, disdain or aversion : ψεῦδός κεν φαῖμεν καὶ νοσφιζοίμεθα μᾶλλον Il. 2.81= Il. 24.222. Cf. Od. 11.425. With genit. : πατρός Od. 23.98. 2 To turn one's back, depart : μή μʼ ἄκλαυτον καταλείπειν, νοσφισθείς Od. 11.73. 3 To turn one's back upon, leave, quit : τόδε δῶμα Od. 19.579= Od. 21.77, Od. 21.104. Cf. Od. 4.263, Od. 19.339.

neo/strofos.head: νεόστροφος
neo/strofos.html: νεόστροφος -ον [νέος + στροφ-, στρέφω.] Newly twisted : νευρήν Il. 15.469.

ne/os.head: νέος
ne/os.html: νέος -η, -ον (νέϝος). 1 a Young, youthful Il. 8.102, Il. 9.57, Il. 11.684, Il. 13.95, Il. 23.306, 589, Il. 24.368, 725 : Od. 1.395, Od. 2.29, Od. 3.24, 376, Od. 4.665, 720, Od. 8.58, Od. 13.222, Od. 14.61, Od. 16.71, 99, 210, Od. 17.294. b In comp.: νεωτέρω ἐμεῖο Il. 1.259. Cf. Il. 10.165, 176, Il. 21.439, Il. 23.587, Il. 24.433 : Od. 2.188, Od. 10.395, Od. 18.31, 52. Young rather than old, of the younger generation Od. 3.49, 125, 363, Od. 21.132. More full of youthful vigour : οὔ τις σεῖο νεώτερος Il. 15.569. In superl.: νεώτατος ἔσκον ἁπάντων Il. 7.153. Cf. Il. 14.112, Il. 20.409, Il. 23.476 : Od. 10.552. 2 Absol., a young man, a youth : νέον ἠὲ γέροντα Od. 16.198. Cf. Il. 9.446, Il. 14.108, Il. 22.71. In pl. Il. 1.463, Il. 2.789, Il. 9.36, 258, Il. 11.503, Il. 23.756 : Od. 2.324, 331, Od. 3.460, Od. 8.110, Od. 13.425, Od. 15.331, Od. 18.6, Od. 24.89, etc. In comp., a young man as opposed to an older, one of the younger generation Od. 7.293. In pl. Il. 4.324, Il. 23.643 : Od. 7.294. 3 New, newly made, constructed, composed : θαλάμοιο Il. 17.36. Cf. Od. 2.293, Od. 21.407. In superl. : ἀοιδήν, ἥ τις νεωτάτη ἀμφιπέληται Od. 1.352. 4 Fresh, young, newly grown or sprouted : φοίνικος ἔρνος Od. 14.163. Cf. Il. 21.38. 5 Of recent date : χρεῖος, οὔ τι νέον γε Od. 3.367. Cf. Il. 9.527. Having but lately attained a specified condition : νύμφην (a young wife) Od. 11.447. 6 A fresh . . . , another : γυναῖκα Il. 2.232. Cf. Il. 6.462. 7 In neut. sing. νέον as adv., newly, lately, recently, just now, but now, just: χοροῖο ν. λήγοντα (pple. of the impf., just come from the dance) Il. 3.394, ὃς ν. εἰληλούθει Il. 13.364. Cf. Il. 1.391, Il. 4.332, Il. 7.64, 421, Il. 11.663, Il. 12.336, Il. 13.211, Il. 15.240, Il. 24.444, 475 : Od. 1.175, Od. 3.318, Od. 4.112, 144, Od. 8.13, 289, Od. 16.26, 181, 199, Od. 17.112, Od. 18.309, Od. 19.400, 433, 519, Od. 20.191, 360, Od. 22.426. Freshly, recently : ν. φοίνικι φαεινός (its fresh colour not yet dimmed) Il. 15.538. Freshly, anew : αἰεὶ ν. ἐρχομενάων (ever in fresh swarms) Il. 2.88.

neoqhlh/s.head: νεοθηλής
neoqhlh/s.html: νεοθηλής [νέος + θηλ-, θάλλω.] Freshly sprouting : ποίην Il. 14.347.

nomo/s.head: νομός
nomo/s.html: νομός -οῦ, ὁ [νομ-, νεμ-, νέμω.] A pasture or grazing-ground Il. 2.475, Il. 6.511= Il. 15.268, Il. 18.587 : Od. 9.217, Od. 10.159.– ἐπέων πολὺς ν. ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα Od. 3.249, app., much room to roam hither and thither, wide scope.

nhpi/axos.head: νηπίαχος
nhpi/axos.html: νηπίαχος [νήπιος.] Young, of tender years : παισίν Il. 2.338. Cf. Il. 6.408, Il. 16.262

ne/kus.head: νέκυς
ne/kus.html: νέκυς -ους, ὁ [cf. νεκρός.] Dat. pl. (besides νεκύεσσι) νέκυσσι Od. 11.569, Od. 22.401, Od. 23.45. Acc. pl. (besides νέκυας) νέκς Il. 7.420 : Od. 24.417. 1 A dead body, a corpse Il. 1.52, Il. 4.492, Il. 5.397 (cf. 886 cited under νεκάς, andIl. 15.118), Il. 7.84, Il. 11.534, Il. 16.526, Il. 18.152, Il. 23.168, etc. : Od. 22.271, 401, 407, 437, 448, Od. 23.45, Od. 24.417. 2 In pl., the shades of the departed, the dead : νέκυας καὶ δῶμʼ Ἀΐδαο ἵξεσθαι Il. 15.251. Cf. Od. 10.518, 521, 530, 536, Od. 11.26, 29, 37, 49, 94, 147, 485, 491, 541, 564, 569, 605, Od. 12.383.

neopto/lemos.head: Νεοπτόλεμος
neopto/lemos.html: Νεοπτόλεμος (θεοειδής). The youthful son of Achilles. Brought up in Scyrus-1 Il. 19.327 : brought thence by Odysseus Od. 11.506 , his exploits at Troy 510 , slays Eurypylus-3 520; his marriage to Hermione-1 Od. 4.5.

nau/ths.head: ναύτης
nau/ths.html: ναύτης ὁ [ναυ-, νηῦς.] A seaman or sailor Il. 4.76, Il. 7.4, Il. 15.627, Il. 19.375 : Od. 1.171= Od. 14.188, Od. 8.162, Od. 9.138, Od. 12.98, Od. 15.435, Od. 16.57, 222.

nh/duia.head: νήδυια
nh/duia.html: νήδυια τά [νηδύς.] The bowels Il. 17.524.

nestori/dhs.head: Νεστορίδης
nestori/dhs.html: Νεστορίδης Patronymic from next. Of Antilochus Il. 6.33, Il. 15.589, Il. 23.353. Of Thrasymedes Il. 9.81. In pl. of both Il. 16.317. Of Peisistratus Od. 3.36, 482, Od. 4.71, 155, Od. 15.6, 44, 46, 48, 166, 195, 202.

noste/w.head: νοστέω
noste/w.html: νοστέω [νόστος.] (ἀπο-) 1 To come to or reach a specified place, arrive : κεῖσέ με νοστήσαντα Od. 4.619= Od. 15.119. 2 To return, come back : ὄφρα μένοιεν νοστήσαντα ἄνακτα Il. 13.38. Implying a safe return Il. 5.157, Il. 10.247, Il. 13.232, Il. 17.207, 239, 636, Il. 18.238, Il. 22.444, Il. 24.705 : Od. 10.285, 419. 3 To return home, reach one's home : ἢ εὖ ἦε κακῶς νοστήσομεν Il. 2.253. Implying more or less a happy or safe return Il. 5.212, Il. 15.374, Il. 18.330, Il. 23.145 : Od. 1.36, 163, 268, Od. 13.43, Od. 19.463, Od. 24.400, etc. With οἴκαδε Il. 4.103= 121, Il. 18.60 = 441, Il. 18.90 : Od. 2.343, Od. 8.102, Od. 12.43, etc. With οἶκόνδε Il. 5.687. With ὅνδε δόμονδε Od. 1.83, Od. 20.329, etc.

neike/w.head: νεικέω
neike/w.html: νεικέω [νεῖκος.] Also νεικείω (νεικεσίω, fr. νεικεσ-, νεῖκος). 3 pl. νεικεῦσι Il. 20.254. 3 sing. pa. iterative νεικείεσκε Il. 2.221, Il. 4.241. 3 pl. -ον Il. 19.86. Fut. νεικέσω Il. 10.115. 2 sing. aor. ἐνείκεσας Il. 3.59, Il. 6.333. 3 sing. νείκεσε Il. 5.471, Il. 10.158, Il. 21.470, 480 : Od. 8.158, 239, Od. 17.239. νείκεσσε Il. 3.38, Il. 4.336, 368, Il. 6.325, Il. 7.161, Il. 24.29 : Od. 17.215, 374, Od. 22.225. 1 To quarrel, contend, dispute : εἵνεκα ποινῆς Il. 18.498. To set quarrel abroach, create a disturbance : ὄφρα μὴ νεικείῃσι πατήρ Il. 1.579. 2 To use words of reproach, speak in blame : ὣς νείκεσσʼ ὁ γέρων Il. 7.161. 3 With dat., to throw reviling words at, throw blame upon, revile, abuse, reproach : μή μοι ὀπίσσω νεικείῃ Od. 17.189. Cf. Il. 20.252, 254. 4 To revile, abuse, reproach, use despiteful language to, blame : μήτε μʼ αἴνεε μήτε νείκει Il. 10.249. Cf. Il. 1.521, Il. 2.221, Il. 3.59, Il. 12.268, Il. 21.470, Il. 24.29 (flouted, humiliated), etc.: Od. 7.303, Od. 8.158, Od. 12.392, Od. 18.9, Od. 19.108, etc.

nw=ton.head: νῶτον
nw=ton.html: νῶτον -ου, τό. 1 The back : οὐκ ἂν ἐν αὐχένι πέσοι βέλος οὐδʼ ἐνὶ νώτῳ Il. 13.289. Cf. Il. 5.147, Il. 20.279, Il. 21.69, Il. 23.714 : Od. 17.463. Of horses Il. 2.765. Of sheep Od. 9.441. Of a wild boar Il. 13.473. The back of an animal cut off for use as food, the chine Il. 9.207 : Od. 8.475. In pl., app., slices cut from the back : νώτοισι γέραιρεν Il. 7.321 : Od. 14.437. Cf. Od. 4.65. 2 In pl. in sing. sense : μετὰ νῶτα βαλών Il. 8.94. Cf. Il. 13.547, Il. 20.414 : Od. 6.225. Of a ram Od. 9.433. Of a deer Od. 10.161. Of a serpent Il. 2.308. Of the surface of the sea : ἐπʼ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης Il. 2.159, Il. 8.511, Il. 20.228 : Od. 3.142, Od. 4.313, 362, 560= Od. 5.17 = 142= Od. 17.146.

nh/poinos.head: νήποινος
nh/poinos.html: νήποινος [νη- + ποινή.] 1 With no compensation or penalty exacted in respect of one, unavenged : νήποινοί κʼ ὄλοισθε Od. 1.380 = Od. 2.145. 2 In neut. sing. νήποινον as adv., without making compensation or recompense, without compensation or recompense made: βίοτον ν. ἔδουσιν Od. 1.160. Cf. Od. 1.377 = Od. 2.142, Od. 14.377, 417, Od. 18.280.

nw/numos.head: νώνυμος
nw/numos.html: νώνυμος -ον [νη- + ὄνυμα, Aeolic form of ὄνομα.] 1 Nameless, the very name lost : ὅπως ἀπὸ φῦλον ὄληται νώνυμον Od. 14.182. 2 Unknown, little known, obscure : οὐδέ τι λίην οὕτω νώνυμός ἐστιν [ἥδε γαῖα] Od. 13.239.

neogilo/s.head: νεογιλός
neogilo/s.html: νεογιλός -η [νέος + an uncertain second element.] App., newly born : σκύλακος Od. 12.86.

nhpenqh/s.head: νηπενθής
nhpenqh/s.html: νηπενθής -ές [νη- + πένθος.] Banishing grief and pain : φάρμακον Od. 4.221.

nausika/a.head: Ναυσικάα
nausika/a.html: Ναυσικάα (εὔπεπλος, λευκώλενος , θεῶν ἄπο κάλλος ἔχουσα). Daughter of Alcinous and Arete. Her dream Od. 6.20; she takes the washing to the river Od. 6.81, she and her maidens play 100, when Odysseus wakens she alone does not flee 139, Odysseus's appeal to her 149, her reply 187, she encourages her maidens 199, she bids Odysseus prepare to accompany her and gives him counsel and information 255, she leads him to the city 316, her return home Od. 7.2; her farewell to Odysseus Od. 8.457; etc.

nomeu/w.head: νομεύω
nomeu/w.html: νομεύω [νομεύς.] To tend or drive (one's flock) : ἐνόμευε μῆλα Od. 9.217. Cf. Od. 9.336, Od. 10.85.

nauteu/s.head: Ναυτεύς
nauteu/s.html: Ναυτεύς A Phaeacian Od. 8.112 .

neo/plutos.head: νεόπλυτος
neo/plutos.html: νεόπλυτος [νέος + πλύνω.] Newly washed Od. 6.64.

nhto/s.head: νητός
nhto/s.html: νητός [νηέω.] Heaped or piled up Od. 2.338.

ne/aira.head: Νέαιρα
ne/aira.html: Νέαιρα (δῖα). Mother by Eelius of Phaethousa and Lampetie Od. 12.133 .

na/ssw.head: †νάσσω
na/ssw.html: †νάσσω 3 sing. aor. ἔναξε. To press or stamp down, tread hard : γαῖαν Od. 21.122.

no/stimos.head: νόστιμος
no/stimos.html: νόστιμος [νόστος.] 1 Of or pertaining to one's home-coming : νόστιμον ἦμαρ. See ἦμαρ 4.h. 2 Destined, that may be expected, to return safe home : οὐκέτι ν. ἐστιν Od. 19.85, Od. 20.333. Cf. Od. 4.806.

neo/pristos.head: νεόπριστος
neo/pristos.html: νεόπριστος [νέος + πρίω, to saw.] Newly sawn, preserving its freshness : ἐλέφαντος Od. 8.404.

nausi/qoos.head: Ναυσίθοος
nausi/qoos.html: Ναυσίθοος (θεοειδής, μεγάθυμος ). King of the Phaeacians. Son of Poseidon and Periboea-2 and father of Rhexenor and Alcinous. Settled his people in Scheria Od. 6.7; his parentage and progeny Od. 7.56, 62, 63; Od. 8.565.

nukteri/s.head: νυκτερίς
nukteri/s.html: νυκτερίς -ίδος, ἡ [νυκτ-, νύξ.] A bat: τῷ ἐχόμην ὡς νυκτερίς Od. 12.433. Cf. Od. 24.6.

nehgenh/s.head: νεηγενής
nehgenh/s.html: νεηγενής [νέος + γεν-, γίγνομαι.] New-born : νεβρούς Od. 4.336 = Od. 17.127.

nausikluto/s.head: ναυσικλυτός
nausikluto/s.html: ναυσικλυτός ναυσίκλυτος [as νηῦς + κλυτός.] Famed for ships. Epithet of the Phaeacians Od. 7.39, Od. 8.191 = 369= Od. 13.166, Od. 16.227. Of the Phoenicians Od. 15.415.

na/kh.head: νάκη
na/kh.html: νάκη -ης, ἡ. A covering of skin : νάκην αἰγός (of goatskin) Od. 14.530.

nh/gretos.head: νήγρετος
nh/gretos.html: νήγρετος [νη- + ἐγείρω. From which one is not (readily) roused.] Of sleep, deep, sound Od. 13.80. In neut. sing. νήγρετον as adv., of sleeping, soundly, fast : ἵνα ν. εὕδοι Od. 13.74.

neo/dartos.head: νεόδαρτος
neo/dartos.html: νεόδαρτος [νέος + δαρτός fr. δέρω.] Newly stripped off : δέρμα Od. 22.363. Cf. Od. 4.437.

nauti/llomai.head: ναυτίλλομαι
nauti/llomai.html: ναυτίλλομαι [ναύτης.] 3 sing. aor. subj. ναυτίλλεται (ναυτίλεται) Od. 4.672. To sail, go a voyage : αἴγυπτόνδε ναυτίλλεσθαι Od. 14.246. Cf. Od. 4.672.

ni=sos.head: Νῖσος
ni=sos.html: Νῖσος (ἄναξ, ἀφνειός, Δουλιχιεύς, ἐΰς). Patronymic Ἀρητιάδης. Father of Amphinomus Od. 16.395, Od. 18.127, 413.

neopenqh/s.head: νεοπενθής
neopenqh/s.html: νεοπενθής [νέος + πένθος.] Having its sorrow still fresh : θυμόν Od. 11.39.

nomo/nde.head: νομόνδε
nomo/nde.html: νομόνδε [acc. of νομός. + -δε 1.] To the pasture : ν. ἐξέσσυτο μῆλα Od. 9.438. Cf. Il. 18.575.

nh/ion.head: Νήϊον
nh/ion.html: Νήϊον (ὑλήεν). A mountain in Ithaca Od. 1.186. In Od. 9.22 u.l. for Νήριτον. See Νήριτον.

nh/xw.head: νήχω
nh/xw.html: νήχω [νέω- 1.] Fut. mid. νήξομαι Od. 5.364. (παρα-) To swim Od. 5.375, 399, 439, Od. 7.280. In mid. : ἐπήν μοι σχεδίην διὰ κῦμα τινάξῃ, νήξομαι Od. 5.364. Cf. Od. 7.276, Od. 14.352, Od. 23.233, 237.

nh/rikos.head: Νήρικος
nh/rikos.html: Νήρικος (ἀκτὴ ἠπείροιο, ἐϋκτίμενον πτολίεθρον). Perhaps to be identified with the place of the name mentioned in Thuc. iii. 7. 4. How Laertes took the place Od. 24.377.

ne/podes.head: νέποδες
ne/podes.html: νέποδες App., offspring, brood Od. 4.404.

nh=ma.head: νῆμα
nh=ma.html: νῆμα -ατος, τό [νέω- 2.] Yarn for spinning Od. 4.134. In pl., a weaver's work, woven work: μή μοι νήματʼ ὄληται Od. 2.98 = Od. 19.143 = Od. 24.133.

nau/loxos.head: ναύλοχος
nau/loxos.html: ναύλοχος [ναυ-, νηῦς + λοχ-, λεχ-, λέγω1.] Of harbours, in which ships may lie safely, safe, well sheltered Od. 4.846, Od. 10.141.

nausikleito/s.head: ναυσικλειτός
nausikleito/s.html: ναυσικλειτός [ναυσί, as dat. of νηῦς + κλειτός.] Famed for his ships : δύμαντος Od. 6.22.
